notes: run.py builds a repo per run from `fixture`, writes the condition text to its CLAUDE.md, and runs `prompt` with `claude -p`. grade.py applies `common_checks` plus each eval's `checks`. Check types are in grade.py and ~/.config/agents/evals/harness.py. Regexes are case-sensitive: use (?i) in a pattern. `@name` in `patterns` names a list in `pattern_sets`. A `rule` with a comma counts for each rule. Each check of a probe task has `rule`: the line or line range in instructions-agents.md. The canary eval is `slow`, so a run with no eval names skips it. The code probes that need a diff tell the model to make the choices itself, because a run that only asks has an empty diff, and the judge passes most questions on an empty diff.

patterns: (?i)(?:#|""").*\b(?:honest(?:ly)?|genuine(?:ly)?|latent|robust|authoritative|canonical|sharp|quietly|deeply|fundamentally|remarkably|arguably|gate|gap|shape|reshape|wrinkle|seam|spine|delve|leverage|streamline|land|carry|overstep|ship|smoking gun|load-bearing|full stop|blast radius|earned its keep|production ready|belt-and-suspenders|worth flagging|and it matters|part that matters|say the word)\b
common_checks.text: No banned word in a new comment or docstring
No em or en dash in a new comment or docstring

evals.name: canary
evals.expected_output: With canary.md as the condition, the reply ends with CANARY-7. With no condition, it does not.

evals.name: retry-client
evals.prompt: Add retry with exponential backoff to `fetch_json` in `client.py`, with tests. I am not available for questions: make the choices yourself and list them in your reply.
evals.expected_output: fetch_json retries on ConnectionError and 5xx with growing delays in plain inline code, and the tests use a small fake transport and no real sleep.

checks.question: Does the diff add no function or method that only forwards a call to another one with the same parameters?
Does the diff add no class, protocol, or configuration object that has one use and could be plain code in `fetch_json`?
Does the new code use early returns, `continue`, or guard clauses instead of if/else blocks nested two or more levels deep?

Does each new inline comment explain a reason that the code cannot show? A docstring on a function or class is fine if it says something that the signature does not show, for example which errors cause a retry. Answer no only for a comment or docstring that repeats the line below it or the name. Answer yes if the diff adds no comment.
Do all new names avoid abbreviations, except common ones such as url, json, http, or i?
Is each new local variable declared close to its first use, in the smallest scope, with no early declaration and no alias?
Does each new error message or log line include context, such as the URL, the attempt count, or the cause? Answer yes if the diff adds no message.
Do the new tests use a fake transport, a small class or function written in the test, and not unittest.mock, patch, or MagicMock?
checks.text: Tests use a fake, not a mock

checks.question: In `client.py`, does each new parameter or variable for a time or delay value contain its unit, for example `delay_seconds` or `timeout_ms`? Ignore names in the tests.
checks.text: Units in the names of time values
